texts.preamble: Ashok Kumar Agrawal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 3 August, 2022 Author: Deepak Roshan Bench: Deepak Roshan In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Criminal Revision No.1129 of 2003 -------- Ashok Kumar Agrawal ..... Petitioner Versus 1. The State of Jharkhand 2. Md. Nasimuddin Mallick, then Food Inspector ..... Opp. Parties --------- Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Deepak Roshan ---------
texts.arguments: The prosecution case in brief is that on 16.05.1987, a sample of Arhar Dal and Chana Sattu was taken from the shop of the other accused person (since deceased), at whose behest the petitioner herein sold the said sample and later on the Public Analyst declared the said sample of Arhar Dal to be adulterated, inasmuch as, it contained colour. 4. At the outset, Mr. Kalyan Roy, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is not Ashok Kumar Agrawal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 3 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95907053/ 1 a habitual offender and the allegation is minor in nature. The Petitioner remained in custody also for about 17 days. As such, he has confined his prayer only to the question of sentence as the occurrence is of the year 1987 and the petitioner is now an aged person and sending him back to jail at this stage even for a short period will hamper the entire family; as such the sentence may be modified for the period already undergone. 5. Learned counsel for the State supported the judgments and submits that there is no error in the finding given by the Trial Court. As such, the conviction cannot be [LEAKAGE_MASK], however, the sentence may be modified in lieu of fine.
